title: Charges dropped against 10-year-old who brought loaded gun to Jackson Local school - NewsBreak
text: CANTON ‒ Criminal charges have been dropped against a 10-year-old accused of taking a gun to a Jackson Local elementary school and making threats last May. Stark County Family Court Judge Matthew P. Kreitzer dismissed juvenile charges of inducing panic, a second-degree felony, and illegal conveyance of a deadly weapon, a fifth-degree felony, on July 30. The decision was based on an evaluation from a psychologist that said the youth was not mentally competent to stand trial and could not be made competent in time for a trial. Reports presented at the court competency hearing included a statement that the boy had done well on pretrial release, and had support from his parents and grandparents. "I think he's in good shape now," said Seth Arkow, an attorney appointed to represent the boy's interests in court. He said he visited the child at his father's home, and found nothing wrong there. Kreitzer noted that a report about the youth said he watches YouTube videos. He advised the family to be sure he does not view inappropriate content. "Watch what he watches on social media," he told the family. The boy got the loaded .45-caliber gun from his grandparents' home before he took it to Sauder Elementary School in a bookbag on May 19, police said. He was accused of making threats against another student and the school resource officer. According to police, the school resource officer confronted the third grader and took control of the firearm. The officer secured the weapon without harm to any students or staff.
